clue.text: Edgy striker, in this case?

parts.note: an edgy striker is a sharp-bladed weapon such as a sword or knife, and the case is the scabbard that holds it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Edgy' looks like 'nervous', but it means having a cutting edge: the striker is a blade, and the case is what it is kept in.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard-like cover that encloses a blade when it is not in use.

clue.text: Composer associated with worldly neighbours

parts.note: the worldly neighbours are the other planets of our solar system, set to music in a famous orchestral suite

explanation.walkthrough: 'Worldly neighbours' sounds like people next door; it means the planets near Earth, the subject of the English composer's suite The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav, the English composer, wrote The Planets, an orchestral suite portraying Earth's planetary neighbours.

clue.text: Excellent meal Braid ordered

indicators.note: the letters of meal and Braid are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone praises a fine dinner arranged by a person called Braid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a diner placing an order; it signals rearranging MEAL and BRAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthy of admiration, so very good indeed: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bird we see circle round point

parts.note: a hoop is a circle of wood or metal
a round shape is the letter O
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sees a bird circling around a spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we see' simply links definition to wordplay; 'circle round' looks like one action but gives two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A crested pinkish bird of Europe, Asia and Africa, named for its call.

clue.text: Tom leads a search in the burial place

indicators.note: the cat goes in front of the rest, leading it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: A man named Tom guides a search party through a burial vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' reads as a man's name but is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground cemetery of tunnels with recesses for tombs, as in Rome.

clue.text: Exact reference found in works of Hardy — or Scott

definitions.text: Exact reference found in works of Hardy — or Scott

parts.words: Exact reference found in works of Hardy — or Scott
parts.note: both Thomas Hardy and Walter Scott wrote novels divided into sections and also poetry, so their works hold both

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a precise citation, originally of the Bible, also literally describes what both writers produced: prose books in sections and poems.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a precise citation of the source, giving full authority for a statement.

clue.text: The whole drink agreement is about settled

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits

indicators.note: the word for agreement goes around the word for settled

parts.note: ay (aye) is a word of agreement, yes
lit means alighted, settled as a bird does

explanation.surface: An entire drinks deal has been settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts AY around LIT to make ALITY after TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The entirety of something, every part taken together.

clue.text: Chesterton's cad and coward (in contrast with tea)

definitions.text: Chesterton's cad and coward (in contrast with tea)

parts.words: Chesterton's cad and coward (in contrast with tea)
parts.note: in G. K. Chesterton's poem The Song of Right and Wrong, one hot drink is a cad and coward while tea is a gentleman

explanation.walkthrough: A literary allusion: Chesterton's comic poem scorns this drink as 'a cad and coward' and praises tea as 'a gentleman at least'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate drink, which the poet mocks against the gentlemanly brew from China.

clue.text: Snail-like A50 columns dispersed

indicators.note: the letters are scattered and so rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Columns of traffic on the A50 road disperse at a snail's pace.
explanation.walkthrough: A50 looks like the British road; it is A plus L (Roman 50), and with COLUMNS 'dispersed' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails belong to the phylum of soft-bodied shelled invertebrates, so this adjective describes them.

clue.text: In the tropics it grows ostentatious

definitions.meaning: a tropical tree with brilliant scarlet flowers, the royal poinciana

explanation.definitionFit: A tropical tree with flame-red flowers; also showy, flashy or extravagant in manner.

clue.text: Fiery mount?

parts.note: a mount is a horse to ride, and a young spirited one is fiery; the name is also that of a famous revolver that fires

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiery mount' suggests a volcano; it is a spirited young male horse, which also shares its name with a gun maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A young male horse, often lively, and also the brand of revolver that is fired.

clue.text: Jack West enters a kind of plant

indicators.note: the sailor and the direction go inside the word for a kind

parts.note: a sort is a kind or type
a jack is a sailor, as is a tar

explanation.surface: A man called Jack West comes upon a particular type of plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack West' reads as a person's name; Jack is TAR, West is W, both entering SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Any of several plants with star-shaped flowers, such as stitchwort.

clue.text: Alliance has some way to go

definitions.meaning: a union of parties or clubs for a common purpose
an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.definitionFit: An association of states or sports clubs; also an old unit of distance of roughly three miles.

clue.text: Restrain poor dog beginning to bark

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel, a worthless dog

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop a wretched dog from starting to bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to bark' sounds like the dog starting up; it gives just B.
explanation.definitionFit: To check or hold back, as with a rein on a horse.

clue.text: What the speaker gives

parts.note: the speaker might be a loudspeaker or an orator; either way it produces spoken sound

explanation.walkthrough: 'speaker' could be a piece of audio kit, but it is simply a person talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken word or statement, the act of expressing something in speech.

clue.text: Economize about Tommy's shelter

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Tommy is slang for a British soldier, who sheltered in a dugout ditch in the First World War

explanation.surface: Cutting costs on the soldiers' accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Tommy' (Tommy Atkins) is a British private soldier; his First World War shelter was a TRENCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut back spending, reducing costs.

clue.text: Description of Flashman's finishing school?

parts.note: Flashman, the bully of Tom Brown's Schooldays, finished at Rugby School by being thrown out for drunkenness

explanation.walkthrough: A 'finishing school' sounds like a place for social polish; here it is how Flashman's schooling ended: he was expelled from Rugby, as told in Tom Brown's Schooldays.
explanation.definitionFit: Being formally thrown out of a school, which is how Flashman's time at Rugby ended.

clue.text: Dealer appears to manage to be in credit

indicators.note: the word for manage sits inside the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit in accounts
to handle is to manage or cope with

explanation.surface: A trader seems able to keep his account in the black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be in' puts HANDLE inside CR, the bookkeeping abbreviation for credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in specific goods, such as a ship's supplies; once a candle-maker.

clue.text: Shorten piano pieces by an Arcadian shepherd

indicators.note: the letters are broken into bits and reassembled

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cut short the piano pieces written by a shepherd in Arcadia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano pieces' suggests music; 'pieces' rearranges SHORTEN with P. Strephon is the Arcadian shepherd of Gilbert and Sullivan's Iolanthe.
explanation.definitionFit: The shepherd lover in Sidney's Arcadia and the Arcadian shepherd hero of Iolanthe.

clue.text: To bet gives us a kick

definitions.meaning: a kick of a ball dropped from the hands, in rugby or American football

explanation.definitionFit: A wager, or to gamble; also a drop-free kick of a ball from the hands.

clue.text: Unseemly rows involving players?

definitions.meaning: public displays of temper, embarrassing quarrels
divisions of a stage play, each with its cast of actors

explanation.definitionFit: Noisy public fusses; also the episodes of a play in which actors perform.

clue.text: Where doors are secured by screws?

definitions.text: Where doors are secured by screws?

parts.words: Where doors are secured by screws?
parts.note: screws is slang for warders, who lock the cell doors in a jail

explanation.walkthrough: 'screws' looks like hardware fixings; in British slang a screw is a prison officer, who locks doors.
explanation.definitionFit: A jail, where warders (screws in slang) keep cell doors locked.

clue.text: How unsuccessful was the shopkeeper, getting an old Italian coin

definitions.meaning: read as sold nought: the shopkeeper had no sales at all
a former Italian copper coin of low value

explanation.definitionFit: Split as 'sold O', the shopkeeper sold nothing; also a small coin once used in Italy.

clue.text: He makes entertaining use of cords

definitions.text: He makes entertaining use of cords

parts.words: He makes entertaining use of cords
parts.note: the cords are vocal cords, and using them to entertain means performing songs

explanation.walkthrough: 'cords' suggests rope or string; they are the vocal cords.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer, who entertains by using the voice.

clue.text: Hit out at singularly bad beer

definitions.meaning: to take a swinging blow at
an old word for thin or poor beer; singularly means in the singular form

explanation.definitionFit: To take a sweeping blow at; also, in the singular, an old name for weak, inferior beer.

clue.text: Colourful part of Manila

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for a dye; the clue's adjective points to its use for colouring

indicators.note: only a portion of the letters of the city name is taken

explanation.surface: A vivid district of the Philippine capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' takes four letters from inside Manila.
explanation.definitionFit: A West Indian shrub yielding indigo dye, so a source of colour.

clue.text: Embarrassing any girl, it's disastrous for a 23

indicators.note: the letters are put into disarray, as if flustered

parts.note: taken as written, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Embarrassing a girl would be a calamity for a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embarrassing' rearranges ANY GIRL and ITS; 23 refers to the answer at 23 across, VOCALIST, who would be silenced.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the voice box causes hoarseness, a disaster for anyone who sings for a living.

clue.text: Concerning food supplied in resort

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a course is a part of a meal served

explanation.surface: A remark about the meals served at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place; it means a fallback option.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turned to for help, a fallback option, as in 'a last resort'.

clue.text: Barber perhaps is a 23?

definitions.meaning: the Barber of Seville, Figaro, is a role that is sung in opera
refers to the answer at 23 across, a performer of songs

explanation.definitionFit: Figaro, the operatic barber, is a baritone role performed by a vocal artist; also the same as the answer at 23.
